The controlling ownership interest means ownership of, or entitlement to, more than 25% of the shares or capital or profit of the company.

citations.title: CDD for Individual Customers (Pages 8-12)
citations.excerpt: Customer Due Diligence for individuals requires verification of identity using Officially Valid Documents (OVD)... Passport, Driving License, Voter's Identity Card, Aadhaar Card. Banks must verify the customer's current address. For low-risk customers, simplified measures may be applied.

citations.title: CDD for Legal Entities (Pages 12-16)
citations.excerpt: For legal entities, banks must obtain Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association, Board resolution for account opening, PAN of the entity, and proof of registered office address. The bank must identify the beneficial owners controlling 25% or more of the entity.

citations.title: Record Keeping (Pages 20-22)
citations.excerpt: Records of transactions must be maintained for a minimum period of five years from the date of the transaction. Records pertaining to the identity of customers must be preserved for at least five years after the business relationship has ended.

inferred_points.point: If the bank must preserve customer identity records “for at least five years after the business relationship has ended,” then closure/exit processes must include a mechanism to mark the relationship end-date and retain identity records for the required post-closure period (rather than deleting them at closure).
supporting_definitions: Records pertaining to the identity of customers must be preserved for at least five years after the business relationship has ended.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.excerpt: "Beneficial Owner" means the natural person who ultimately owns or controls a client or the person on whose behalf a transaction is being conducted. For a company, it is the natural person who, whether acting alone or together, or through one or more persons, exercises control through ownership or who ultimately has a controlling ownership interest. The controlling ownership interest means ownership of, or entitlement to, more than 25% of the shares or capital or profit of the company.

citations.title: CDD for Individual Customers
citations.excerpt: Customer Due Diligence for individuals requires verification of identity using Officially Valid Documents (OVD). The following documents are accepted as OVD: Passport, Driving License, Voter's Identity Card, Aadhaar Card. Banks must verify the customer's current address. For low-risk customers, simplified measures may be applied.

citations.title: CDD for Legal Entities
citations.excerpt: For legal entities, banks must obtain Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association, Board resolution for account opening, PAN of the entity, and proof of registered office address. The bank must identify the beneficial owners controlling 25% or more of the entity.

Trust T has 4 beneficiaries; one beneficiary has 8% interest in the trust; trustee is a corporate trustee.

Identify all Beneficial Owners you must determine for X, and explain why each qualifies (ownership vs control vs 'senior managing official' fallback). Also list whose CDD you must perform (customer, BOs, authorised signatories, POA holders, etc.) and what evidence you'd rely on.

For Company X as a ‘legal person’ customer, analyse BO identification where shareholding is below the prescribed percentage thresholds but there are shareholder agreement rights amounting to ‘control’. Clarify whether Company A’s director-appointment and veto rights trigger BO identification of the relevant natural person(s) behind Company A, and how Trust T’s BOs are determined (trustee/settlor/protector/beneficiaries with prescribed interest), including treatment of a corporate trustee and a beneficiary with 8% interest. Then list the CDD/KYC obligations for each category of person (customer, BOs, authorised signatories, beneficial owners of the trust, and any power-of-attorney/mandate holders) and the acceptable Officially Valid Documents / beneficial ownership declarations to rely on.

Identify the specific definitions and carve-outs applicable to ‘beneficial owner’ and ‘controlling ownership interest/control’ for a company customer with dispersed shareholding and a trust shareholder, and map them to the verification steps: (a) BO determination for Company X (ownership vs control), (b) BO determination for Trust T as a shareholder (including corporate trustee and beneficiaries), and (c) application of the ‘senior managing official’ approach if BO cannot be established.
